definition: Direct marketing is a form of promotion sent straight to selected individuals through personal communication channels such as phone calls, text messages, or emails. In the gambling context, this kind of targeted contact may be especially influential because it reaches people directly rather than through general advertising.

reasons: The claim that this may be influential “because it reaches people directly rather than through general advertising” is not supported in the packet (the packet does not contrast direct marketing with “general advertising”).

The definition’s gambling-specific wording “especially influential” is not directly phrased as an evidence-backed conclusion about influence; the packet says “Combining promotional marketing with the use of direct communication channels is likely to be an especially potent form of influence,” which is more specific than the definition’s broader explanation.

The final clause adds an unsupported comparison to “general advertising”; the packet only says direct communication channels can make marketing especially potent, not that it works by contrast with general advertising.

The definition makes a broader contextual claim about gambling-specific influence that is only partly supported; the packet supports that direct marketing may be potent and that studies in gambling are limited, but not the broader explanatory framing given here.
